known_facts_book1: A Royal Princess who grew on the central Royal Bush in the Royal Garden of the Rose Kingdom, and is a distant cousin of Ozma of Oz.
Is the only royal on the bushes ripe enough to pick; all the other growing royalties are still green and lifeless.
Is picked by Betsy and Shaggy, who each take an arm and a twist of her feet frees her from the branch; she steps down and thanks them.
Is refused as Ruler by her own subjects because they want a King and will have no girl rule over them.
Is driven out of the Rose Kingdom with the others by the Roses' thorns and over the drawbridge across the boundary gulf.
Ceases to be a fairy the moment she is exiled and will never again be more than a mere mortal, which is why she eats ordinary food on the journey.
Asks the field-flowers, whom Files calls her second-cousins, which way leads to Ruggedo's kingdom, and every stem bends and nods three times to the right.
Is transformed by Ruggedo into a fiddle and restored by being touched to Quox's pink ribbon.
Offers her kiss to break the Ugly One's charm, as a Mortal Maid who was once a Fairy, but it fails.
Is sent to Oogaboo with Files at the end, because Ozma will not separate two who have become such good friends.

known_relations_book1.Files: The Private of Oogaboo who becomes her constant companion and goes to Oogaboo with her.
known_relations_book1.the Roses: Her rebellious subjects, who refuse a girl Ruler and drive her out.

known_relations_book1.Ozma: Her distant cousin, who sends her to Oogaboo with Files.
known_relations_book1.Ruggedo: The Nome King who turns her into a fiddle.

known_facts_book1: A funny little man in a rose-colored costume with ribbons at his knees and elbows and a bunch of ribbons in his hair, with small twinkling eyes and a puckered, deeply lined face.
Rules the Rose Kingdom himself because no man-rose on the Royal Bushes is ripe enough to pick, the last Ruler having got mildewed and withered before his time.
Quotes page thirteen of his little book of Law: any stranger who enters the Rose Kingdom shall at once be condemned by the Ruler and put to death.
Falls at Shaggy's feet in adoration the moment he sees the Love Magnet, but insists that no true man neglects his duty for the sake of love — and drives them out anyway.
Is kicked out of the greenhouse door by Hank without touching the ground.
Lets down the drawbridge over the boundary gulf for the outcasts and draws it up again behind them.

known_relations_book1.the Roses: His subjects and, in the matter of the Ruler, his masters.
known_relations_book1.Ozga: The Princess he must expel from her own kingdom.
known_relations_book1.Shaggy Man: Loves him on sight because of the Love Magnet, and expels him regardless.
known_relations_book1.Hank: The mule that kicks him out of the greenhouse.

known_facts_book1: Magnificent rosebushes in a great crystal greenhouse, each bearing on its central stem one splendid Rose with the face of a lovely girl in its center.
Named individuals among them are a dainty Moss Rose, a delicate Tea Rose and a Jacque Rose.
Sleep with drooping heads and closed eyelids until Hank's bray wakes them, and are terrified of his voice.
Declare that only Roses are allowed in the Rose Kingdom and that strangers must be cast back into the sea.
Are entirely unmoved by the Love Magnet, because their stems have thorns but no hearts — the one thing in the book the Magnet cannot win.
Refuse Ozga because they want a King and will have no girl rule over them, and will wait until a man-rose is ripe enough to pick.
Drive the outcasts out of the garden and the greenhouse with the sharp thorns hidden beneath their draperies of green leaves.
